account: The RL-Zero-Math weight change is small (about 0.25 % of each matrix's norm) with about 12 % of its squared norm in the top 8 singular directions of each matrix, which read a residual subspace the base's own step-by-step text already drives 8-11x more than random and write directions the base's next layers amplify (1.67x random); Think-SFT's no-reward change lies in this subspace on both sides (4.8x chance on the input side) and Code-RL's about 5x more than Think-SFT's, so any training on long deliberation concentrates there, even with an LM-judge reward (top-8 share 0.127 vs 0.135).

Added to the base at 1.5x, these 8 directions alone match RL on hard328 (200.25 vs 200.0 right per 4-sample draw; equal-norm random rank-8 159-167, cued base 164) because they carry RL's own route preference, which lowers the per-step slip rate rather than only making answers finish: on problems the cued base finishes wrong they add 13.5 points (RL 12.3), on its 0-of-4 problems they take 0.88 of RL's per-sample gain, and where both fail their wrong answers agree with RL's more than the base's do.

The gain sits in layers 0-21 and in the rank of the edit, not its norm: bands 0-10 and 11-21 each add about 20 of RL's ~40 hard328 points and nearly add up, layers 22-31 carry only the finishing and boxing habit and alone add nothing (166; 155 at 3x), one direction per matrix gives half (181 at 1x, 168 at 3x), and another model's top-8 edit helps only as far as it lies in Math 3.1's top-8 subspace (Math 3.0 182, IF-RL 155, Think-SFT's top-8 at 1x breaks the model), with no gain beyond RL's level (theta 1.25: 450 vs 457 on MATH-500).

Changes made only at inference reach most of the gain because the base already has this deliberative mode and the three-token cue switches it on (a plain answer that happens to open with 'Okay' is right as often), the same stage RL's first 100 steps install (step 100 is within 1.4 points of the cued base, at its cap-hit rate and with its vote gain), which takes MATH-500 from 224 to 410 against RL's 457-463 and gives 77 % of RL's gain on non-math questions.

What remains, about 10 points at T 1.0 and 22 at T 0.6 (where 52-63 % of the base's long answers are loops), is per-step reliability: 81 % of it lies on problems the base solves in some sample, and because the base's wrong answers scatter (same-problem pair agreement 0.26) a vote over 4 recovers 0.07-0.11 per contested problem, but it cannot reach the 26 of 36 problems where the base has no right sample, while RL, already reliable, gains only 2.8 points from voting.

On code the input side is shared but the written directions are reward-specific: Code-RL's 8 directions raise the pass rate of finished answers 7 points over random while Math's add 1.5, and their fixes are problems the base passes in other samples (0.75), so the edit carries RL's reliability without RL's problem-specific losses (on problems the base passes and RL-Code fails it passes at a base resample's 0.45, not RL's 0.22).
